- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.23) — model tends to lag or overshoot upward trends.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially < -0.16) — model fails to capture downward momentum or mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.61 or +0.23) — model overreacts, then corrects too late.
- Underreact to sustained negative sentiment — model holds too close to prior levels, missing downward drift.
- Mean reversion bias: model often overcorrects after strong moves, especially in 30-day horizon — forecast tends to “bounce back” too early.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts — model reacts 1–2 days after sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns positive.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — model often ignores 3–5 day sentiment trends in favor of 10–15 day patterns.
- Price forecasts should be adjusted downward if sentiment is negative and price is rising — model tends to ignore sentiment when price is trending up.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates — especially if recent price is rising.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overestimating near-term spikes (e.g., +0.61 sentiment) and underestimating long-term mean reversion.
